entries.description: Organize Terraform projects with separate files: main.tf (resources), variables.tf (input declarations), outputs.tf (outputs), providers.tf (provider config), versions.tf (version constraints), locals.tf (computed locals), and a modules/ directory for reusable components.
decision_rules: Separate concerns into dedicated files — do not put everything in main.tf
Place reusable infrastructure patterns in modules/ with their own variables.tf and outputs.tf
tradeoffs: More files increase organization but require tooling (terragrunt, workspaces) for multi-environment management
anti_patterns: Putting all resources, variables, and outputs into a single main.tf
Hardcoding environment-specific values inside resource definitions

entries.concept: Secure remote state with S3 + DynamoDB backend
entries.description: Configure Terraform backend with S3 (encrypted, KMS key) and DynamoDB for state locking. Required fields: bucket, key, region, encrypt=true, kms_key_id, dynamodb_table. Prevents concurrent state modifications and encrypts sensitive state data at rest.
decision_rules: Always use a remote backend for team environments — never rely on local state
Enable encrypt=true and provide a KMS key for state file encryption at rest
Use DynamoDB for state locking to prevent concurrent terraform apply conflicts
tradeoffs: S3 backend requires the bucket and DynamoDB table to be provisioned before running terraform init
anti_patterns: Committing terraform.tfstate files to version control — state may contain plaintext secrets
Using local backend for shared or production environments
aws_alignment: S3 bucket for state should have versioning enabled and public access blocked
Use a dedicated AWS account for Terraform state storage

entries.description: Mark sensitive variables with sensitive = true to suppress their values in plan/apply logs. Never set sensitive defaults. Inject real values at runtime via environment variables: export TF_VAR_db_password=$(aws secretsmanager get-secret-value ...).
decision_rules: Add sensitive = true to any variable containing a password, token, or key
Inject secrets via TF_VAR_* environment variables populated from a secrets manager at CI/CD time
Never set a default value on a sensitive variable
tradeoffs: sensitive = true hides values in plan output but they are still stored in state — encrypt state
anti_patterns: Passing secrets as CLI arguments (visible in shell history and process list)
aws_alignment: Retrieve secrets from AWS Secrets Manager in CI/CD before running Terraform apply

entries.description: Mark outputs that expose sensitive values with sensitive = true. Non-sensitive outputs (e.g. DB endpoint) can be marked sensitive = false. Sensitive outputs are still stored in state — ensure state is encrypted.
decision_rules: Set sensitive = true on any output that references a password, token, private key, or secret value
Use outputs only for values required by other modules or CI/CD steps
tradeoffs: sensitive = true prevents outputs from being displayed but does not prevent them from being read by a caller module
anti_patterns: Outputting raw DB passwords or private keys without sensitive = true
Exporting secrets via outputs when they can be referenced directly within the same module

entries.concept: VPC with private and public subnets
entries.description: Structure VPC with three layers: public subnets (ALB only, map_public_ip_on_launch=false), private app subnets (ECS/EKS workloads), private data subnets (RDS). Use count and cidrsubnet() for multi-AZ subnet creation. Apply common tags via local.common_tags.
decision_rules: Never assign public IPs to application or database instances — use private subnets
Use at least 2 availability zones for high availability
Set map_public_ip_on_launch=false even on public subnets — assign EIPs explicitly where needed
tradeoffs: NAT Gateway required for private subnet internet egress — adds cost (~$35/month per AZ)
anti_patterns: Placing RDS instances in public subnets
Using a single availability zone for production VPC
aws_alignment: Use aws_nat_gateway in public subnets for outbound internet access from private subnets
Use VPC Endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB to avoid NAT Gateway costs for AWS API traffic

entries.description: Security groups should allow only required ingress traffic from specific sources (other SGs, not CIDRs where possible). Egress should be restricted to required protocols/ports. Never allow 0.0.0.0/0 ingress on ports 22 (SSH) or 3306 (MySQL). Add description to every rule.
decision_rules: Reference other security groups (not CIDR blocks) for ingress between AWS services
Restrict egress to HTTPS (443) for services that only call external APIs
Add a description field to every ingress/egress rule for auditability
tradeoffs: SG-to-SG references are region-specific — cross-region traffic requires CIDR-based rules
anti_patterns: ingress from_port=22 cidr_blocks=["0.0.0.0/0"] — exposes SSH to the internet
egress from_port=0 to_port=0 protocol=-1 cidr_blocks=["0.0.0.0/0"] — allows all outbound traffic
aws_alignment: Enable VPC Flow Logs to audit security group traffic
Use AWS Config rule restricted-ssh to detect open SSH rules

entries.concept: IaC security scanning with tfsec and Checkov
entries.description: Integrate IaC scanners into CI/CD: tfsec (tfsec . --severity HIGH), Checkov (checkov -d . --framework terraform --check CKV_AWS_*), Terrascan (terrascan scan -t terraform -d .). Use aquasecurity/tfsec-action in GitHub Actions workflows.
decision_rules: Run tfsec or Checkov in CI/CD and fail the pipeline on HIGH severity findings
Use --check CKV_AWS_* to apply AWS-specific CIS benchmark checks with Checkov
tradeoffs: Scanners may produce false positives for intentional deviations — use .tfsec/config.yml or checkov skip annotations to document exceptions
anti_patterns: Running terraform apply without IaC security scanning in CI/CD
Suppressing all scanner warnings without documentation
aws_alignment: AWS Security Hub integrates with Checkov results via SARIF format

entries.description: Define common_tags in locals.tf and apply via tags = local.common_tags on every resource. Standard tags: Environment, Project, ManagedBy (terraform), Owner, CostCenter. Use merge(local.common_tags, {...}) to add resource-specific tags.
decision_rules: Apply common_tags to every taggable AWS resource for cost allocation and governance
Use merge() to extend common tags with resource-specific tags rather than duplicating the base set
tradeoffs: Tags are eventually consistent on some AWS services — not suitable for real-time access control
anti_patterns: Hardcoding tag values individually on each resource instead of using locals
Not tagging resources — prevents cost attribution and governance enforcement
aws_alignment: AWS Cost Explorer and Cost Allocation Tags require consistent tagging
AWS Config can enforce mandatory tags via required-tags managed rule

entries.concept: Use pinned versions for Terraform modules
entries.description: Always pin module sources to a specific version when using Terraform Registry or Git sources. Example: module vpc with source terraform-aws-modules/vpc/aws and version = "5.5.1". Never use "latest" or an unpinned source.
decision_rules: Pin module version to a specific release tag — never omit the version field
Update module versions deliberately after reviewing the changelog for breaking changes
tradeoffs: Pinned versions require manual updates — use Dependabot for Terraform to automate version bump PRs
anti_patterns: Omitting the version field on registry modules — pulls the latest version on every init
Using a git branch reference (ref=main) instead of a tag — non-deterministic builds
